subject: ICAEW Budget 2027 Commentary: Will stronger public finances mean more secure Malaysian households?
label: reject
bodyText:
Dear Wayne,

As coverage of Budget 2027 moves from the announcements to what they mean
for Malaysians, one question deserves a closer look: will the improvement
in public finances translate into greater financial security for households?

The attached commentary from ICAEW members at Folks DFK and BDO Malaysia
explores where policy could make a practical difference, particularly for
families whose incomes leave them outside assistance thresholds but still
struggling with everyday costs.

Among the issues they raise:

 - *Who qualifies for help:* Why household size, dependants and location
 should carry more weight, and how a small pay rise can leave a family worse
 off if it means losing assistance.



 - *What keeps living costs high:* Why cash aid needs to be complemented
 by affordable housing near transport and employment, and childcare that
 enables parents to work.



 - *How families build financial security: *Ways to help first-time
 buyers save for a deposit without taking on excessive debt, while
 encouraging more consistent retirement savings.


Featuring Datuk Peter Lim, Group Managing Partner of Folks DFK Group, and
BDO Malaysia’s David Lai and Jen Shaun Wong, the commentary offers a
household perspective on Malaysia’s fiscal progress, with specific
proposals for addressing the pressures that remain.

We hope you would consider carrying this for your Budget follow-up
coverage. You’re welcome to use the commentary in full or draw on the
members’ views for a broader story. Happy to coordinate any follow-up
questions or interviews as well.

Thanking you in advance!

Warmest regards,
Michelle

The Malaysian AI orchestration and governance company brings its approach
to agentic business process reengineering to China as part of its
international growth.
[image: Glem.ai CEO Ryan Tay (left) at the signing with the Jianwai
Sub-district Office in Beijing, marking Glem.ai's incorporation in China.
(Photo by Jianwai Sub-district Chamber of Commerce)]

KUALA LUMPUR and BEIJING, 7 October 2026. Glem.ai, a Malaysian enterprise
AI orchestration and governance company, today announced its incorporation
in China and the opening of an office in Beijing’s Central Business
District. The new entity, 北京革睿科技有限公司 (Beijing Gerui Technology Co. Ltd.),
establishes a permanent base for technology collaboration and business
development in China.

The expansion follows Glem.ai’s recognition as a winner of ITEC 2025 and is
supported by Beijing’s Chaoyang District government. In September 2026,
Co-Founder and CEO Ryan Tay and Co-Founder and CTO Alvin Chua joined the
Malaysian delegation to China initiated by YB Lee Chean Chung.
[image: CEO Ryan Tay and CTO Alvin Chua with YB Lee Chean Chung in Beijing
as part of the China-Malaysia Tech Delegation]

“Our ambition is to build a global enterprise AI company from Malaysia,
helping organisations transform how they operate while retaining control of
their technology and data,” said Ryan Tay. “Our Beijing base brings us
closer to China’s strengths in AI and industrial innovation. We want to
build lasting partnerships here, develop solutions together and take
Malaysian innovation into enterprise markets around the world.”

Glem.ai plans to work with Chinese enterprises and technology partners,
initially focusing on manufacturing and healthcare. The Beijing presence
will also support opportunities to bring solutions developed through these
collaborations to Malaysia and other international markets.
Redesigning business processes for agentic AI

Glem.ai’s approach begins with the design of the business process.
Introducing AI into an existing workflow can amplify inefficiencies and
expose weaknesses when the underlying process is flawed. The company helps
enterprises rethink how work should be carried out, where agents can take
responsibility and where human oversight remains essential.

Its team delivers this agentic business process reengineering using the
Glem platform and PMAL, a methodology it developed around Plan, Monitor,
Action and Learn. PMAL guides the redesign of operations from the ground
up, incorporating agentic AI into the process itself and using operational
feedback to improve it over time.

“AI can scale the weaknesses of a flawed process just as quickly as it
scales the work,” said Alvin Chua. “We redesign the process from the ground
up, then provide the orchestration, governance and infrastructure
enterprises need to trust it. Our ambition is to make AI dependable enough
to take on complex operational responsibilities under clear human
authority, across entire organisations.”

Applications span Agentic MES, which brings AI agents into manufacturing
execution, and Agentic Vision, which applies AI to CCTV and visual
monitoring, alongside workflows across other enterprise functions.
[image: Glem.ai CEO Ryan Tay (left) and CTO Alvin Chua (right) speaking at
the signing ceremony in Beijing. (Photo by Jianwei Sub-district Chamber of
Commerce)]Supporting continuous AI transformation

As AI adoption grows, departments increasingly build their own applications
or introduce different agents, models and tools. Glem provides a shared
orchestration and governance layer through which these initiatives can be
connected and managed, giving organisations room to innovate while
maintaining oversight.

The platform provides visibility and traceability into which AI systems and
agents are being used, the data they access and their associated costs.
Access controls and full audit records support accountability, while
deployment inside an organisation’s own infrastructure allows it to retain
sovereignty over its data. This gives enterprises a foundation for
extending their AI transformation as new use cases and technologies emerge.

The Glem.ai team has worked with leading organisations across oil and gas,
manufacturing, healthcare and government. Its enterprise delivery
experience includes projects that achieved a 90% reduction in processing
time and over US$40 million in cost savings. The company has a presence and
active projects across Malaysia, the Philippines and the Middle East, with
Beijing now providing a base in China.

subject: Data centers to use 31% of Peninsular Malaysia's power by 2035: Delta's efficiency figures from DCW Asia

Dear Editor,

Malaysia's Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry projects
that data centers will take 31% of electricity demand in Peninsular
Malaysia by 2035, up from 7% this year
<https://www.nst.com.my/amp/news/nation/2026/07/1477411/data-centre-power-demand-peninsular-malaysia-surge-31pct-2035>.
Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil said in September that the country's
AI ambitions must be matched by sustainable use of power and water
<https://thesun.my/news/ai-ambitions-sustainable-power-water-use-fahmi/>. *How
efficiently data centers use power is now part of the national
conversation.*

Delta Electronics, which opened an office in Iskandar Puteri, Johor, in
July, unveiled new data center technology at Data Center World Asia 2026 in
Singapore. Attached is the release, which I hope you'll share with your
readers.

Two figures stand out. Delta’s new 800VDC system, built for Nvidia’s Vera
Rubin platform, converts power from AC to DC at up to 98% efficiency, so
less energy is lost along the way. Separately, Delta’s prefabricated
containerized data center reaches a PUE as low as 1.19 (v the theoretical
best of 1.0). The release contains the full technical specs.

*Given Delta’s involvement in Malaysia and the impact of this technology,
we hope you will share this with your readers.*

Please find the release images here (link expires 10 Oct):
https://we.tl/t-nPCPHhWWFiFaPx3W

I look forward to hearing back from you.

---

*Delta Electronics Unveils AI Modular Data Center with 800 VDC *

*In-Row Power for NVIDIA Vera Rubin and Microgrid Solutions at *

*Data Center World Asia 2026*



*SINGAPORE, September 29, 2026 *– Delta Electronics, a global leader in
power management and smart green solutions, is attending Data Center World
(DCW) Asia 2026 with its new AI Modular Data Center (AI MDC) and Microgrid
Solutions to accelerate the deployment and enhance the energy efficiency
and resilience of AI infrastructure. The prefabricated AI MDC integrates
next-gen 800 VDC In-Row Power and liquid cooling systems for the fast
deployment and scalability of AI data centers based on NVIDIA Vera Rubin
architecture. The Microgrid Solution integrates Delta’s renewable energy,
energy storage, and Solid Oxide Fuel Cell (SOFC) systems, as well as Solid
State Transformers (SST), which are essential to directly convert medium
voltage power to 800 VDC for the AI factories of the future.



“AI workloads are scaling faster than most data centres were designed to
handle, while their demands can be increasingly unpredictable. This means
infrastructure planning must move from reactive to integrated and
future-ready,” said Jason Yuan, President, Southeast Asia & ANZ, Delta
Electronics. “Our AI Modular Data Centers and Microgrids, both part of our
Grid-to-Chip Solutions portfolio, are ideal to help our clients across
Southeast Asia deploy and power their future-ready AI data centers.
Moreover, Delta’s solutions are engineered for energy efficiency,
reliability and performance, while providing the flexibility to adapt to
changing workloads and infrastructure demands.”



Visitors can expect interactive showcases spanning Delta Electronics’ AI
infrastructure portfolio, including its AI Modular Data Center designed for
scalability, flexibility, and compatibility, high-voltage direct current
(HVDC) 3.6MW in-row coolant distribution unit (CDU) technology to help
manage the thermal demands of high-density AI workloads. The showcased 800
VDC In-Row Power architecture features 660kW output power, up to 98% AC-DC
efficiency, 480kW capacity in battery backup units (BBU), and aluminium
capacitors to optimize GPU workloads in next-generation AI data centres. In
addition, Delta’s prefabricated AI Containerized Data Center (CDC)
Solutions deliver up to 60 kW per rack of AI compute within the footprint
of a single parking space, as well as a seamlessly integrated Liquid-to-Air
CDU system to achieve a PUE as low as 1.19.



The unveiled Microgrid Solution demonstrates how on-site energy generation
resources, energy storage, power conversion, and the new solid state
transformer (SST) can support greater power resilience, efficiency and
flexibility. Through real time coordination of multiple energy
sources, uptime and power quality are maintained during grid connection
delays or off-grid operation, with SOFC providing reliable on-site power
24/7. Its prefabricated DC-coupled architecture combines SSTs, DC/DC
converters and dynamic energy support to reduce conversion stages, enabling
the system to respond to fluctuating AI loads while supporting scalable
deployment.



At the board-level, Delta’s thermal management solutions include a
dedicated state-of-the-art cold plate for NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, with the
latest microchannel and multi-impinging flow design.



*See the Future of AI Infrastructure Live at DCW Asia 2026*



Delta Electronics will showcase the In-Row Power at DCW Asia 2026, taking
place from 29–30 September at the Marina Bay Sands Convention Centre, Level
1, Singapore, at Booth D10. Sakda Sae-Ueng, SEA & Oceania Data Center
Business Platform Head, will also be headlining the Data Centre World
Keynote Theatre at 10:25am on Day 1, where he will discuss Delta
Electronics’ collaboration with NVIDIA and the roadmap for 800VDC power
architecture.



Singapore and the Southeast Asia region are increasingly viewed as a
regional hub for next-generation AI infrastructure, with operators across
the region under pressure to deploy at a pace and density that did not
exist a cycle ago. Delta Electronics helps customers respond to this shift
with integrated power, cooling and energy infrastructure engineered to
support the rapid evolution of AI workloads, while providing the
flexibility, efficiency and resilience needed to remain future-ready and
accelerate the transition towards more sustainable data centers.



*ABOUT DELTA ELECTRONICS INT'L (Singapore)*

The company is a wholly owned subsidiary of Delta Electronics, Inc.



*ABOUT DELTA*

Delta, founded in 1971, and listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange
(code:2308), is a global leader in switching power supplies and thermal
management products with a thriving portfolio of IoT-based smart
energy-saving systems and solutions in the fields of industrial automation,
building automation, telecom power, data center infrastructure, EV
charging, renewable energy, energy storage and display, to nurture the
development of smart manufacturing and sustainable cities. As a world-class

leverages its core competence in high-efficiency power electronics and its
ESG-embedded business model to address key environmental issues, such as
climate change. Delta serves customers through its sales offices, R&D
centers and manufacturing facilities spread over close to 200 locations
across 5 continents.



Throughout its history, Delta has received various global awards and
recognition for its business achievements, innovative technologies and
dedication to ESG. Since 2011, Delta has been listed on the Dow Jones

*New portfolio and strengthened channel network mark a new chapter for
Xerox in Malaysia*
[image: First from left: Keith Leong, Regional Sales Director, APC, Lexmark
alongside executive representatives at the launch of the new Xerox and
Lexmark A4 printer lineup.]

*PETALING JAYA, 8 October 2026 – Xerox* has returned to Malaysia with a new
portfolio of Xerox-branded A4 colour printers and multifunction printers,
opening a new chapter for the company following its integration with
Lexmark.

Unveiled at Le Méridien Petaling Jaya, the devices are among the first
hardware offerings introduced under the unified Xerox brand following the
integration. By combining Xerox’s global technology and services
capabilities with Lexmark’s established local presence, channel
relationships and market expertise, the company is strengthening its
ability to serve customers and partners across Malaysia.

The launch responds to the needs of increasingly hybrid and distributed
workplaces, where organisations require technology that is secure, easy to
deploy and well suited to smaller workgroups and shared office environments.

Through the integration, Xerox is bringing together capabilities across *print,
IT infrastructure and intelligent digital services*, giving organisations a
broader portfolio to support more digital and connected workplaces.

The event also showcased Xerox and Lexmark’s existing A3 and A4 portfolios,
demonstrating the breadth of workplace technology now available to
customers in Malaysia.

An auspicious lion dance marked Xerox’s return to Malaysia. The company
also recognised its three local distributors—*Digital Paper Sdn Bhd, ATM
Trading (M) Sdn Bhd and Tec D Distribution (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd*—for their
continued commitment to customers, partners and business growth in the
country.

*“Malaysia is an important market for Xerox and our re-entry through the
integration with Lexmark is a significant milestone. It combines the
strength and heritage of Xerox with Lexmark’s established local presence
and channel relationships, giving us a stronger platform to serve
customers, enable our partners and build sustainable growth in Malaysia,”
said Keith Leong, Regional Sales Director, APC.*

*New A4 portfolio for evolving workplaces*

Central to Xerox’s return is a new range of *A4 colour printers and
multifunction printers* for small workgroups and hybrid environments. The
devices provide reliable print and scan capabilities without the need for
dedicated IT support.

Compact form factors are combined with simplified setup, security and
connectivity features:

*Ease of use:* Intuitive interfaces, simplified setup and support for the
Xerox® Easy Assist App and Xerox® Print and Scan Experience App help users
install, manage, print and scan with ease.*Performance:* The portfolio
supports reliable, consistent everyday use across a range of small
workgroup needs, including more demanding environments. *Security:*
Built-in security features help protect devices, documents and network
access, with integrated post-quantum cryptography support for future-ready
protection against evolving cyber threats.*Compact design:* Space-efficient
form factors suit small offices and shared workspaces.*Sustainability:*
Energy-efficient operation and more than 50% post-consumer recycled plastic
content support Xerox's commitment to responsible innovation.

*Four new Xerox A4 colour devices *for* Malaysia*

The launch portfolio comprises the *Xerox C240 colour printer and the Xerox
C245, C303a and C305ae colour multifunction printers*.

Together, the four models offer straightforward deployment, dependable
everyday performance and secure operation across a range of small-workgroup
environments.

*Availability and enquiries*

The new models, together with Xerox and Lexmark’s existing A3 and A4
portfolios, are available through Xerox and its authorised channel partners
in Malaysia.

For enquiries, interested parties can connect with an authorised dealer
through the *Find a Dealer* <http://Find%20a%20Dealer%20page> page on the
company’s website or contact Xerox-Lexmark at *salesapc@lexmark.com*
<salesapc@lexmark.com>.

Dear Editor/Journalist, We missed you at the exclusive media event at
Thrive Together 2026: Triple Alliance Mental Health Symposium. During the
event, Professor Dato' Dr Adeeba Kamarulzaman highlighted the importance of
treating mental health as a shared responsibility rather than an individual
burden, while highlighting the Triple Alliance's commitment to advancing
student well-being through cross-institutional collaboration between Monash
University Malaysia, Sunway University, and Taylor’s University. The
symposium also explored key issues including Malaysian youth mental health,
neurodiversity inclusion, trauma-sensitive campus practices, and
student-led initiatives aimed at fostering healthier, more resilient
communities. Please find the press release attached and appended below for
your reference, along with event photos available via the link provided
below.
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XS3XXNOR7WgOxV3Vt1wGATvhrbGLEDB6?usp=sharing.
Should you require any additional information or images, please feel free
to reach out. Thank you for your time and continued support.

Subang Jaya, 29 September 2026 – As mental health continues to be a
critical priority in higher education, Monash University Malaysia is
leading the Triple Alliance’s flagship mental health initiative, Thrive
Together 2026, bringing together Monash University Malaysia, Sunway
University, and Taylor’s University to strengthen mental health awareness,
support and inclusion across higher education.

Held at Monash University Malaysia, the two-day initiative brings together
more than 1,700 staff and students, mental health professionals, educators
and community partners through expert discussions, practical workshops and
interactive activities focused on building supportive and inclusive campus
communities.

Keynote speaker Professor Dato’ Dr Andrew Mohanraj Chandrasekaran,
President of the Malaysian Mental Health Association, addressed the topic
on “Mental Health Amongst Youths in Malaysia”.

“Our internal survey found that 16% of respondents reported experiencing
cyberbullying, underscoring the importance of building supportive
environments where young people feel connected, heard and able to seek help.

“Social connection is fundamental to mental wellbeing, while resilience is
not about simply enduring difficulties or trying to cope on our own. It is
about recognising and accepting when we are struggling, having the
confidence to set boundaries and say no to what is affecting us and
understanding that it is okay to ask for help.

“Most importantly, we need to encourage young people to seek and accept
support early, before challenges escalate into more serious concerns. By
equipping young people with these skills and fostering stronger support
networks, we can help them recover from adversity, move forward and thrive.”

The initiative is one of the first major programs to take shape following
the formal launch of the Triple Alliance earlier this month, putting its
commitment to collaboration and student wellbeing into practice. Thrive
Together goes beyond raising awareness by bringing together mental health
professionals, educators and students to share knowledge and practical
approaches for recognising and responding to mental health needs.

The staff mental health symposium features sessions on supporting
neurodivergent students, building trauma-sensitive environments, and
developing effective listening and helping skills. A dedicated forum also
brings together representatives from the three universities to discuss ways
to strengthen student mental health support.

For students, interactive outreach activities focus on emotional awareness,
mindfulness, self-care and help-seeking, alongside mental health screening
and suicide prevention awareness initiatives delivered with community
partners. Skills-based workshops cover areas including art therapy,
building emotional awareness and resilience, and supporting friends in
distress.

Professor Dato’ Dr Adeeba Kamarulzaman, President and Pro Vice-Chancellor
of Monash University Malaysia, emphasised the responsibility universities
hold in supporting student wellbeing:

"At Monash University Malaysia, placing student experience and well-being
at the heart of our mission is central to what we stand for. Just weeks
after launching the Triple Alliance, Thrive Together demonstrates that
commitment in action. Mental well-being directly drives how students learn,
thrive, and build community. By uniting the strengths of our three
universities alongside external experts, we are actively fostering an
environment where support is accessible, stigma is removed, and every
student knows they are never facing challenges alone."

She also highlighted the thinking behind the symposium’s title, noting that
institutional responses to mental health have traditionally focused heavily
on crisis intervention. While rapid crisis care remains essential, she
said, true wellbeing requires a broader approach that includes proactive
support systems, inclusive spaces free of stigma, and evidence-based
strategies that enable individuals to thrive.

Other speakers include Jovial Teo, Counselling Psychologist and
Neurodivergent and Special Needs Specialist at Joyful Soul Psychology
Centre, Singapore; Dr Nicole Chen, Clinical Director of HEAL Systemic
Therapy Centre; and Nadzreen Hakimi Bin Mohd Yazid of the Malaysian Mental
Health Association.

The initiative also brings together counselling and student-support
representatives from Monash University Malaysia, Sunway University and
Taylor’s University for a dedicated forum on strengthening mental health
support across their respective campus communities.

Through these discussions and activities, Thrive Together is equipping
university communities with practical knowledge and skills to support
students, encourage early help-seeking and foster more inclusive
environments. The collaboration with external mental health partners
further strengthens the initiative’s focus on practical support and shared
responsibility for student wellbeing.

Thrive Together 2026 reflects the Triple Alliance’s commitment to turning
collaboration into meaningful action, beginning with initiatives that
support the wellbeing, inclusion and success of students across its three
university communities.

*Fast Retailing Announces Record Performance for Fifth Consecutive Year*
UNIQLO operations in all regions report revenue and profit gains, as more
customers globally discover the value of LifeWear

*October 8, 2026 – Tokyo / Malaysia* - Fast Retailing Co., Ltd. (“Fast
Retailing” or the “Group”; HK stock code: 6288) today announced the
financial results for its 2026 fiscal year, reporting a record-high
consolidated business performance. This marks the fifth year of consecutive
record performances. The strong results were underpinned by UNIQLO
operations in all regions reporting year-on-year revenue and profit gains,
following the opening of high-quality stores that effectively convey the
value of LifeWear, and the strategically enhanced coordination of products,
store displays, and customer communications.

The Group’s consolidated revenue in the year to August 31, 2026, rose to
¥3.9633 trillion, a 16.6% increase from the previous year, with business
profit totaling ¥718.4 billion, a robust 30.4% year-on-year increase.
Finance income recorded a net gain of ¥59.3 billion, consisting of ¥52.2
billion in interest income and ¥7.1 billion in translated foreign exchange
gains on foreign-currency denominated assets. As a result, profit before
income taxes increased to ¥802.5 billion, rising 23.4% year on year, and
profit attributable to owners of the Parent expanded to ¥542.5 billion, an
increase of 25.3%.

The year-end dividend per share was expected to rise to ¥530, which - when
added to the ¥320 interim dividend - would generate a scheduled annual
dividend of ¥850; an increase of ¥350 from the previous year.

The Ministry of Digital, via MyDIGITAL Corporation, has launched the Rakyat
Digital Global Learning Pass, giving *100,000 Malaysians* access to digital
and AI learning opportunities through Coursera as part of Malaysia’s AI
Nation 2030 ambition.



Open to eligible Malaysians with a MyDigital ID, the government-funded
initiative provides *three months of complimentary access* to more than *16,000
courses and Professional Certificate programmes* offered by leading
universities and industry experts worldwide. Courses cover high-demand
areas including AI, technology, data science, business and digital literacy.



The initiative comes as *41% of Malaysia’s core skills are expected to
change by 2030*, highlighting the growing need for accessible, continuous
learning. Early results point to strong interest, with *12,900 learners
enrolling in 43,000 courses. *



Key highlights include:

 - 100,000 licences being rolled out in phases, subject to eligibility
 and availability
 - Strong learner engagement recorded in Selangor, W.P. Kuala Lumpur,
 Johor, Pulau Pinang and Perak
 - Popular courses include Google’s AI Fundamentals, Foundations: Data,
 Data, Everywhere and Foundations of Project Management, reflecting demand
 for practical, job-relevant skills

KUALA LUMPUR: Sanct Social founder Sion Abednego has shared three lessons
from the fifth Global Digital Trade Expo (GDTE) in Hangzhou, China, held
from 23 to 26 September 2026, which he attended as a member of the
Indonesian business delegation.

The lessons come from two days of business-matching sessions with Chinese
technology companies and from the exhibition floor, where AI accelerator
cards, voice assistants, industrial AI models and smart glasses were on
show and on sale.
[image: The]

*Lesson one: support from research to launch*

Sion said the Chinese government supports its start-ups from research and
development through to launch, which in his view is why their products
reach the market at prices that are hard to match: on the production side
the companies have little to lose.

"Their prices are hard to match not only because labour there is great and
affordable. The bigger reason is who carries the risk at the start.
Research and production trials are paid for before a product reaches the
market, so the selling price does not have to cover that risk any more. For
a young company that is a lesson about how an ecosystem works, more than a
lesson about cost," he said in a statement.
[image: One of the AI exhibits on the floor of GDTE 2026, Hangzhou.]

*Lesson two: one task per city*

Each city in China, he said, has its own assigned field of innovation to
grow fast, so Hangzhou is not Shenzhen or Shanghai, and is not meant to be.
A wall at the expo spelled out Hangzhou's six fields in one word, WEALTH:
wellness, education, art, life, transport and health.

*Lesson three: technology and culture side by side*

The visit fell on the Mid-Autumn Festival, 25 September 2026, celebrated in
China with mooncakes and with families gathering to look at the full moon.
He said the streets were still full at half past eleven at night, shops
open and pavements busy until two in the morning, and that on Hefang
Street, the city's old street, a street painter drew visitors' portraits on
paper fans a short walk from halls full of AI hardware.
[image: The exhibition hall of GDTE 2026 at the Hangzhou Grand Convention
and Exhibition Center.]

"The technology at the expo was remarkable, and the way they back their
start-ups is worth studying. But what I remember most is a whole city going
outside to look at the moon together. In Hangzhou people quote the city's
own poet, Su Shi: 但愿人长久，千里共婵娟. Dàn yuàn rén chángjiǔ, qiānlǐ gòng chánjuān.
It means: may we live long, and though a thousand miles apart, share the
same bright moon. That is the feeling Sanct Social is built for," he added.

The greeting heard everywhere that night: 中秋快乐. Zhōngqiū kuàilè. Happy
Mid-Autumn Festival.

*On the river*

At the delegation dinner on a boat after the GDTE closing ceremony, the
towers on both banks lit up into one giant screen, and nearly everyone on
deck watched it through a phone. He said Sanct Social was built for the
opposite: at 6pm the people a user is close to gather in one place,
together, even when one of them is across the Causeway and the rest are at
home.
[image: The Hangzhou riverside at night, the towers lit up as one
screen.][image:
The delegation dinner on the river, Hangzhou]

*What comes next*

One partnership from the business-matching sessions is being followed up,
and Sanct Social plans to return to China in 2027 to see the prototype. "We
came home with homework, not with an announcement. Hangzhou taught us that
good products come from long support and from people willing to sit at the
same table," Sion said.

learn from mistakes, and prepare for examinations with clearer direction.

turning feedback into progress.

EdPrep.ai acts as a "Second Brain" tutor, guiding learners through
explanations, practice questions, and step-by-step reasoning via an
approachable on-screen AI companion. Supporting this workflow is Smart
Learning Memory, an engine that synthesizes a student’s study history,
practice results, feedback, and milestones. This creates total continuity
between study sessions, tailoring support around individual strengths and
areas needing attention.

EdPrep.ai supports preparation for local exams including the SPM, STPM,

notes, key takeaways and action items.

devices and manage policies remotely.

subject: Press Release and Photo - Allianz Life encourages Malaysians to turn breast cancer awareness into action

bodyText:

Dear Editor,



The Breast Cancer Awareness Month is a timely reminder that knowing the
risks is only the first step. Taking action through regular screenings,
informed conversations and preventive care is equally important.



Yet fear, uncertainty, and misconceptions can often prevent individuals
from seeking medical advice or going for health screenings, even when early
detection can make a meaningful difference.



In conjunction with the Breast Cancer Awareness Month this October, Allianz
Life Insurance Malaysia Berhad (Allianz Life) is encouraging Malaysians to
take proactive steps towards protecting their health and wellbeing through
early detection, preventive care and informed health decisions.



Allianz Life Chief Executive Officer, Giulio Slavich, said awareness should
be the starting point for action.



“Fear should never be a barrier to seeking help. Whether it starts with a
conversation, a screening or a medical consultation, taking that first step
can make all the difference. We want Malaysians to know that support is
available and that they do not have to face the journey alone,” he said.



”Through Allianz Pink October and Movember 2026, we hope to create a
welcoming space where people can learn from experts, ask questions and feel
more confident about taking positive action for their health and future,”
Giulio added.



Please see attached press release and photo for your perusal.



Thank you.





*Best Wishes,*

*Gary Mark Nagan*

*Allianz Malaysia Berhad*

subject: [PRESS RELEASE] Novo Nordisk rebrands as ‘Novo’ in Malaysia amid growing focus on chronic disease prevention

bodyText:
Dear Editor,

Hope all is well!

*Novo Nordisk enters a new chapter in Malaysia with the rollout of its new
global corporate brand, “Novo”*, alongside a wider shift in how the company
wants to approach chronic disease and everyday health.
[image: image.png]

The change comes at a particularly relevant time for Malaysia. According to
the National Health and Morbidity Survey
<https://iku.gov.my/images/nhms2023/fact-sheet-nhms-2023.pdf> 2023, 54.4%
of Malaysian adults were overweight or living with obesity, while 15.6%
<https://www.dosm.gov.my/site/downloadrelease?id=statistics-on-causes-of-death-malaysia-2025&lang=English>
had diabetes, with cardiovascular disease continuing to account for a
significant share of the country’s health burden.

Rather than being purely a visual rebrand, the new direction centres
on *“Lasting
Health Starts Now”* and reflects a broader move towards looking at chronic
disease through the *whole person* including not only clinical indicators,
but also everyday factors such as nutrition, sleep, activity, stress,
family circumstances and whether people feel able to seek help early. In
Malaysia, the story also touches on a wider healthcare conversation
around prevention,
earlier intervention, stronger primary care and public-private collaboration,
areas highlighted under the country’s Health White Paper
<https://www3.moh.gov.my/moh/resources/Penerbitan/Penerbitan%20Utama/Kertas%20Putih%20Kesihatan/Kertas_Putih_Kesihatan_(ENG)_compressed.pdf>
.

Among the perspectives featured in the release:

 - *Professor Dr Jeyakantha Ratnasingam, Senior Consultant
 Endocrinologist and Head of Endocrine Unit at Universiti Malaya, discusses
 why obesity and diabetes often sit alongside interconnected cardiovascular
 and metabolic risks, and why earlier conversations matter.*
 - *Emeritus Professor Dr Chan Siew Pheng, Consultant Endocrinologist,
 shares why managing chronic disease extends well beyond clinic visits and
 into people’s everyday lives.*
 - *Tee Loong Tek, Head of Market Access and Public Affairs, Novo
 Malaysia, speaks about what the company’s next chapter means locally and
 the role of partnerships across Malaysia’s healthcare ecosystem.*

The company is also introducing *The Novo Way*, a refreshed corporate
culture built around customer obsession, competitiveness, clarity, and care
& integrity.

consideration in this link here
<https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AaC3uuUC-PClRzYpFz9_fIyhhLJaRJYc?usp=sharing>.*

*If useful for a broader feature, we’d also be happy to explore an
interview or further commentary around Malaysia’s chronic disease
landscape, earlier health intervention and how healthcare can become more
relevant to people outside the clinic setting.*

Thank you as always and hope this may be of interest for your consideration.

Dear Editor,

Hope you’re having a great day,

What happens after a breast abnormality is detected and how much can the
quality of intervention and coordination between specialists shape what
happens next for the patient?

[image: image.jpeg]

Hospital Picaso, BD, and the College of Radiology Malaysia come together
for Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) signing ceremony, symbolising their
shared commitment to advancing breast intervention and strengthening breast
cancer care in Malaysia.

As Breast Cancer Awareness Month puts breast health in the spotlight this
October, Hospital Picaso, BD (Becton, Dickinson and Company) and the
College of Radiology Malaysia are taking the conversation beyond awareness
by strengthening the expertise and capabilities behind breast cancer care.

This comes at a critical time for breast cancer care in Malaysia, where 50.5%
of staged female breast cancer cases
<https://nci.moh.gov.my/images/pdf_folder/SUMMARY-OF-MALAYSIA-NATIONAL-CANCER-REGISTRY-REPORT-2017-2021.pdf>
were diagnosed at Stage III or IV, highlighting the continued need to
strengthen capabilities across the breast cancer pathway from diagnosis and
intervention through to treatment and coordinated care.

A key part of the collaboration is the launch of the BD Breast Academy
Malaysia Chapter in collaboration with Hospital Picaso, which aims to train
at least 100 breast surgeons, breast radiologists and radiographers annually.
The programme will bring together healthcare professionals through hands-on
workshops, masterclasses, clinical mentorship, case discussions and
observerships, while Hospital Picaso will be developed as a Breast
Intervention Centre of Excellence and training hub.

For Breast Cancer Awareness Month, the partnership offers a timely
perspective on an important part of the breast cancer conversation that
happens behind the scenes to strengthen the healthcare professionals,
clinical expertise and collaboration that support better patient care.

For full information of the partnership, please find the press kit attached
here

with the full press release and accompanying photos.

Should you be keen to take the story further, we’d also be happy to
coordinate follow-up interviews with the relevant clinical or
organisational spokespeople around late-stage breast cancer diagnosis,
breast intervention, multidisciplinary care and the importance of
strengthening specialist training in Malaysia.
